newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai, Singapore launch industrial joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Thai, Singapore launch industrial joint venture.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and his Singapore counterpart, Goh Chok Tong, on Monday witnessed the signing of an 18 billion baht ($720 million) industrial estate joint venture in southeastern Thailand.

JTC International Pte Ltd, a wholly owned unit of Jurong Town Corp of Singapore, teamed up with Eastern Sugar Co Ltd of Thailand to build the venture's planned 1,133-hectare industrial park in Rayong and Chonburi provinces.
The park, called the Thai-Singapore 21 Industrial Estate, will be the biggest Thai-Singapore joint venture for the past several years.
A statement issued by the two companies said it will host factories and other manufacturing facilities worth 120 billion baht when it is completed in eight years.
JTC International holds a 40 percent stake in the venture, named KK-JTCI (Thailand) Co Ltd, with the rest of its equity owned by Eastern Sugar, a unit of Thailand's diversified KK Group.
JTC International said it had undertaken 15 industrial estate projects in seven Asian countries.
